methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $43M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
FleetZero is a Series A transportation company founded by Steven Henderson and Mike Carter that has raised $43M to date. The relevant comp universe consists of six private frontier-technology firms in the transportation sector, including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, REGENT Craft, and Beyond Aero. No public transportation peers were available for direct comparison.

Given the early-stage profile and sparse comparable data, only one valuation method proved applicable. The stage-progression approach uses the $43M total raised as a proxy for current value and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression, yielding an implied valuation of $86M. The peer-median method was not applicable because the available transportation comparables lacked sufficient depth at the same or adjacent stage with matching valuation tier—only three same-sector peers exist in the dataset, insufficient for a reliable median calculation.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $73M (low) to $99M (high), with a median of $86M. This range reflects heavy reliance on a single methodology and thus carries material uncertainty. Key risks to valuation include the thinness of comparable data at FleetZero's stage and the heterogeneity of the transportation tech sector, which spans vehicle platforms, logistics, and infrastructure. A more robust assessment would benefit from additional private comp data or revenue/growth metrics to anchor stage-progression assumptions.
